I mean, it, it, uh, sounds real exciting and and there's a possibility. I mean, we can't say that it isn't because we don't know what it is. Uh, we've talked to Dr. Kaplan quite a bit on this subject, uh, probably, probably know him from the, uh, University of California. Uh, he thinks that they're either some kind of a, possibly a new meteor that we are not familiar with, or, uh, some phenomena that's related to the aurora. Uh, he, he, he claims that he can duplicate this color in his lab and I, I'm not, uh, sure of just exactly how he does it. I believe he uses, uh, well, I don't know, I won't say. I've got a report but I don't want to quote something I don't know about. But anyway, he can duplicate this color, and he believes that that's what it is. Now, uh, as I say, that is a definite division of these things. I mean, they, they definitely exist and our problem is to find out, really find out what they are. If they're some kind of phenomena, why then we can turn it over to the astronomers and let them take it. Uh, if they should happen to come from Russia, why then we better start finding out what they're trying to do on it.

(Question from audience)

- "How many of these green light reports do you have?"
- "We have quite a few, sir. I'd hate to say, I mean, I couldn't tell you exactly a number, but they started out in, I believe, '49. Yes, sir. There was a big outbreak of them in '49, and

they seem to appear in January or in December and January, in that period between the years. And they coincide with a meteor shower that occurs at that time. I don't believe I know, remember the name of it is, but for a long time, they tried to tie them in with that meteor shower, but just recently now, within the last year, they've begun to occur more on a, over the whole year instead of coming at at one time. OSI, Dr. LaPaz worked for OSI in '49 on these and they tried to come up with a conclusion, they couldn't. They've also spent a lot of time trying to find any fragments and have never been successful. I mean, they've been able to triangulate these things and get a heck of a lot of reports on people who have seen them or seen one of them and then work their triangulation like they do on large meteors, but they've never been able to find any parts. They wanted us to fire to pick up, put a dust collector on a B-29 and try to fly through the area right after these things occurred, try to pick up any dust that they might have left in the upper atmosphere, but they didn't find anything at all that would indicate that anything unusual was going on. So, we're up against a stone wall on these things too. I mean, all we've got is just people's ideas. We've got no proof as to what they actually may be. Now, we've, one of our approaches on this thing is going to be the use of diffraction gratings on cameras. This is Dr. Kaplan's idea. He says that we can, and I mean, I shouldn't say he says, we know that we can take a very inexpensive camera and put a diffraction grating on it and give them to these guards around Sandia and White Sands and all these places where the guards are outdoors 24 hours a day. And every time they see something that's unusual, just point the camera at it and take a picture, and then he says that he can take the reading and match them up either by known objects or match them up in his lab and tell us what the composition is of this object that's emitting this light. Now, we haven't, that's just strictly in the planning stage now, we haven't done very much except Dr. Kaplan is now trying to figure out the cheapest camera that he can build for us and the most rugged camera so these guards can throw it around and still get some decent pictures of these objects. Another thing that we've done is recently we've briefed the Air Defense Command on this whole project and have got their cooperation in with their radar scope cameras. As I mentioned before, we have had quite a few unknown radar returns. These things have, the Air Defense Command radars tracked objects going anywhere from 1,000 up to about 3,500 miles an hour. We've never been able to determine, however, that these weren't malfunctions in the radar set or due to some type of atmospheric phenomena. We've tried to get the weather charts at the time or weather conditions at the time this phenomena has occurred and try to correlate that data and show that due to a certain type of weather condition that they had this type of return. Now, we haven't had too much luck on that angle, so now we're going to try to get radar scope cameras and get pictures of this stuff, and then we'll know. Before, we just had the radar observer's interpretation of what he saw on the scope. We think that with pictures, probably we can do a little bit more with this. Now, another step further than that, and we haven't done anything on this except talk about it, and it may get into the point where we are going to

do this, and that is try to put in a long focal length camera, try to match this, a long focal length camera with the radar spinner, so that whenever this radar operator gets a return, all he has to do is poke a button and this camera will take a picture of the area of the sky that the radar spinner is pointing at. And in that, if we get that far, and if we get a bad or funny return, we'll say, an unusual return on a scope, and if we get an image, no matter how big the image is, on the photographic plate or on the film at the same time, why then we can say that this radar operator was actually picking up something. I mean, that would be a great help to us now because we don't know for sure if they're even picking anything up. But that's the next step and it's still in the planning or even it's in the talking stage right now. That's about the main thing we're going to try to do as far as future plans are concerned. We want to get, try to get some concrete data to say that these things exist. Up till the present time, we've got no real proof that anything even exists. The only thing we've got are reports from very reliable people that do have a lot of details in them, but the details aren't the kind that we want. I mean, they don't give us enough data as to the possible performance or anything else that we might need on these objects. The official Air Force viewpoint is that we've got enough good reports from reliable people to be interested in this. We can't back up any of these books by Scully or Keyhoe and say that we know that they're from Venus or that we know they're from Russia or that we even know they exist. I mean, there's a possibility that everything that's being reported is some, is a balloon or is a meteor or ducks or anything you can think of that somebody just saw them from an odd angle or under odd lighting conditions and they look like something else. But it's at the present time, we have enough faith in these people that have been turning in the reports to say that we don't exactly believe them. I mean, we're going to have to get more proof before we can say that everything that's being seen is some known object just viewed under different circumstances.

I could go on for a long time telling you about the good reports we've had. I'd say about 20% of the 800 or 900 reports that we now have just cannot be explained. I mean, you can't say that looks like a meteor. You can't say that that could be a balloon if there's a balloon in the area because it just doesn't tie up. And most of these people that have made these reports are well-established airline pilots, I mean, old pilots who've had a lot of flying time, the people that released these General Mills balloons have seen something, the people at White Sands have seen very odd things, this Dr. LaPaz himself has seen a couple things floating over the mountains down in New Mexico that he didn't, he couldn't explain. And we've got about 20% of our reports are like that, that we just, we can't go up to them and say, 'Now you can't, this can't be, you're nuts.' I mean, that would be our only answer on those. 'You're just crazy.' But you can't go up to anybody and tell them that. I mean, they're, they've seen something and we don't know what it is. Now, some of the big questions that enter our mind on this is one, the no sound business. If it actually exists and there's no, there's some type of propulsion but there's no sound, what could it possibly be? Another big question is, and it's getting into the lines of psychology, why or how could a person look up at night or in the dusk, we'll say, or even in the daytime and see some of

these things that they report? Now, right along those lines, we had, the same time these pictures were taken down in Lubbock, within two or three days of that time, two women were driving along in a car, and all of a sudden they looked out over the Texas plains and they saw this object that they described as being top-shaped, like one of these old-fashioned tops you put a string around and pull, and it was silver and it was hovering along over the prairie. And they drove up, well, they approached it, and as they approached it, why the thing began to take off like that. Well, now we checked on these women and found out that they were just as reliable as your wives or anybody else. I mean, they didn't have any reputation of being habitual liars or stretching stories or anything like that. They were just good old Texas farm wives is all they were. And we questioned them, but that's their story. I mean, they said, 'That's what we saw. We don't know what it was. We're leaving it up to the Air Force to tell us what we saw.' Well, Thunder, we can't tell them. And once again, it goes down back to the point, how much can people imagine? At the same time these Lubbock pictures were taken, in fact, it's the same night, a guard and his wife from the Sandia base in Albuquerque were sitting out in their backyard, and all of a sudden they looked up and they saw this big dark shape go over. And they said that it was, it looked a lot like a flying wing type aircraft, and it was down about 150 feet and it just scared the dickens out of them because it was so low. And they could see little exhaust flames on the back of the airplane. Well, we checked them again and once again, we found out that they're just good, normal people. I mean, the guy's been a guard at Sandia for a good number of years, so he's reliable to that extent. I mean, they don't usually hire psychopathic cases to guard places like Sandia. And just out of curiosity, we sent these pictures down to that guy, and the OSI showed them to him and he said, 'Yeah,' he said, 'that's what I saw, but,' he said, 'it was, these little lights are the exhaust stacks that I saw.' And it happened on the same night that these pictures were taken, just about two hours before these people saw this thing at Lubbock. So, I mean it, it's probably a coincidence, but again, you can't say it's a coincidence. I mean, we can't get enough facts to ever pin it down, but it's one of those things that's just very interesting to work on. I mean, it'll drive you nuts after a certain amount of time, but then we try to keep going on it. That's about all that I had. If you've got any questions, well, we'd be very happy to discuss any aspect of this whole thing with you folks.

(Question from audience)

• "What sort of performance data do you get out of these radar returns?"

• "Uh, it varies. It varies quite a bit. Usually high speed. When I say high speed, I mean anything over 1,000 miles an hour. Uh, they, for a while, we we thought we had it pinned down or our radar people did because the return always went over the station. It came in, went through the ground clutter, practically directly over the station and went out the other side. Now they claim that that was an indication of, uh, something, I'm not sure, uh, interference in their station or something like that. But lately, we, they haven't been doing that. I mean, they'll, they'll come in to the, uh, into the range and they'll maybe make a turn and go out. Now we had one interesting case from New Spay Library and, uh, this

GCA operator was, uh, sitting there looking in his scope and all of a sudden he saw these two objects come in. They were coming in about 4 or 500 miles an hour. And at the same time a C-47 was coming in, he was going to land his 47. Well, he noticed they were on a collision course, so he called the tower and said, 'Tell those two unidentified airplanes they're on a collision course with this 47.' So the tower just called in the blind... The tower said there's no other airplanes out there. The radar man said, 'Yes, there is.' The tower just called in the blind and said, 'Uh, you two unidentified airplanes, you're on a collision course with a 47.' And just as they said that, these two returns made a turn. Now, once again, have we got coincidence or have we actually got something? See, I mean it, uh... Do they speak English? ... So, that's about the only conclusion we can draw, they must speak English. But, uh, that's some of the things we run into. We run into a lot of that kind of stuff where we'll have a lot of small situations that all build up into a big one. And it might be just a coincidence. It might be, we may put our imagination into it unconsciously. Only we, we try to keep away from that. We try to stay right in the straight and narrow. I mean, we don't want to, uh, be influenced either way on this thing. They may be from Mars, but if they are, we don't want to think they are. We don't want to think they're all balloons. I mean, we try to stay right in the middle of the road. Now, we had a real interesting one from, uh, New Jersey, uh, around Sandy Hook and Fort Monmouth here not too long ago. These pilots in a T-33 chased something, and about 10 minutes later, all our radar stations in that area begin to pick these objects up going back and forth all over the skies. And we thought, 'Boy, this is it.' So we tore up there to find out, and boy, the story sounded real fine. These T-33 pilots saw this great big disc-shaped thing over there and he took out after it and he couldn't catch it. And then the radar stations begin to pick up these signals and they were clocking speeds up to 3,500 miles an hour and everything else. Well, it turned out that the pilots had seen a big balloon. It was larger than a normal weather balloon, had been launched at Fort Monmouth. And they were a little bit mixed up with their rate of closure and stuff like that and had seen a balloon. And the radar crews, the first radar crew had picked up a, probably just an ordinary aircraft, but they were giving a demonstration to a bunch of colonels and the operators got a little bit flustered on the whole thing and they couldn't lock in this automatic tracking, so they assumed the thing must be going about 3,500 miles an hour. And it turned out the reason they couldn't lock it in is they were just too excited and got a little bit fouled up on their procedures. And from then on, why they were picking up weather balloons, uh, with these radar reflectors hanging on them and everything else, and the students, incidentally, it turned out they were mostly student radar operators picking this stuff up. The, uh, headquarters had called in and hadn't explained anything. They just said, 'Get on your radar scopes and look for these mysterious objects floating around.' Well, that's all it took for these kids because, boy, they saw everything. Well, what at first appeared to be a very good sighting just all broke down when we get enough facts. Now

maybe they'll all turn out to do that, but so far, we've got an awful lot of them that we can't even come close to explaining."

• "I'd like to, at the risk of repeating, just sum up some of these points. One is, Lieutenant Ruppelt mentioned around 800 cases that we have in our files. We know that that's only a portion of the sightings that have been made. Those are the ones that have managed to be reported to some military base and then through channels get to us. You can read local newspapers almost anywhere in the country, and if you read them over a period of time, you'll find stories on these things that we have not heard of. We've even heard of them in military organizations that have not been reported because I think it's almost a case of the airline pilots that wonder if there isn't something peculiar. For example, I was talking to some people from SAC the other day, and they were telling me about a radar bomb scoring run of a B-29 out at St. Louis. And they were following the B-29 in to the initial point. The operator noticed this plane flying or an object at 48,000 feet. The B-29 was at 25,000 feet. He immediately thought, 'Well, that's possible.' I mean, double harmonics or something, and anyway, he explained it away in his own mind. Well, then the blip started descending on a collision course, and a quick check revealed that it was descending at a rate of something like 1,000 miles an hour. He got a little more concerned, still thought, 'Well, possibly this is either in the radar or in some atmospheric condition.' Well then when the thing broke off and made a turn and then another turn and took the course and disappeared, they just don't know what it is. We find on these radar sightings that you're just left pretty much outside. I mean, you can't really dig in. You haven't got anything because there's so many of them that can be explained as there's a possibility that it is something either in the atmosphere or in the set. We had one good one not too long ago, and one of our electronics people pulled out a textbook and, gee, there was a case written up in the textbook exactly what had been reported to us. A hovering object that made a rapid rate of ascent and then took off on a course. Well, such a thing has occurred apparently because of weather phenomena, been reported and pretty thoroughly written up. So we find that whole area of sightings, I mean we're just left without any answers. One point that was not brought out is our relationship with Battelle."

• "Oh, yes, I forgot to mention... Battelle Memorial Institute. They're one of the contractors who do work for us and... (inaudible) ...They're always silent. They became interested in this when we pointed out to them one day that here's an area in which we've had a lot of problems, and we're looking for help. We don't know the answers. So, one of the things that they hope to do for us is make available to us people who are specialists in various areas. So if we get a case that calls for an astronomer, we can quickly get an astronomer to work on it. Another thing is possibly a clipping service that will bring in a mass of reports we don't have, and if any of them are worth following up, we can. But our problem is just getting facts. We don't have enough facts to do anything other than explain that 80% of these, roughly, are known objects, or possibly. As a matter of fact,

they're not 80% definitely proved, but say 60 definitely. I mean, there's no question in our mind it was a plane or something else. And then, these are rough figures, say 20% that maybe could have been a plane, a balloon, or a meteor. And then there's that 20% like the green fireballs and the lights that we just do not have an answer for. Now, one thing that people have suggested, 'Well, how about a feasibility study?' Well, you, a feasibility of what? The unknown. We're stuck there."

(Question from audience)

• "Have all the intelligence officers of the bases and units been alerted on this and they report everything, or is the military generally alerted to this?"

• "Yes, we, we should have brought that out early. There is a directive from Headquarters, USAF, that establishes a reporting procedure. Now, we felt for a long time, like most directives, particularly if there's no activity on it, people forget about it. I mean, it gets stuck off in the file. We've also felt that it was not a very good one. It had a lot of weak points in it. So we prepared a new directive, and in the meantime suggested that they go ahead and remind all of these people that there is a reporting procedure set up so that it would bring reports in. And the new directive has just recently been coordinated, I believe, hasn't it? It's going back to DOI right now."

• "And it should be out. Now, Lieutenant Ruppelt, in getting around on these cases, of course, does a lot of missionary work because when he hits a base, I mean, he briefs them pretty thoroughly on our problem. And the places he's hit, I'm sure, are well aware of how it's done. I'm equally sure there are a number of these places that just don't know. They probably have a directive somewhere."

• "I was just thinking of my own case. I knew you folks were interested from this association or others, but no still any efficient channel that never heard that there's any interest from..."

• "How about the ground observer corps? They have 100,000 people, don't they? And they're quite active now, but I haven't..."

• "We, they are to a certain extent, sir. We've talked about that quite a bit, and we don't know whether it's worth alerting those people. Now, they're not now on a 24-hour basis. They will, they hope to get them on a 24-hour basis soon. But, we don't know exactly how far to go. I mean, we're afraid maybe if we alert that number of people, then everybody in the United States will get excited again. That's the thing we're trying to keep out of this thing is this excitement business. Now, in two weeks, a week from this coming Friday, Life is coming out with an article on these objects, and we've been working closely with Life, and they're supposedly are going to print what we told them to. I hope they do. They're going to put it on a factual basis. I mean, just about like this briefing. In other words, there may be something to it, but we don't know. And we feel that that report

may tend to take the mysteriousness and hysteria out of the thing and just get people to give us a few reports, you know, people with good common sense instead of all these nut letters that we get occasionally. Another thing, Colonel Kirkland referred to this newspaper clipping service, we hope to get that started before this Life magazine article comes out and keep it going over say a period of a year and see how the peaks in the newspaper publicity correspond with the peaks in this, in the reports that we get. We feel that after Life comes out, why then several other magazines will undoubtedly pick this stuff up. A True magazine is supposed to be coming out with an article sometime within the next couple months. It will be slanted the other way. It's going to be written by one of these science fiction writers, and it should give us no end of trouble. We haven't been able to get True to cooperate with us at all. I mean, I shouldn't say that, they probably would, but their type of magazine, I mean, they sell a sensational item, and they don't, they want to play it up. And then, I believe Look is also thinking about coming out with an article. So, magazines are going to follow Life and we'll probably run into a little bit of flak again on this thing."

(Question from audience)

• "Is it unlikely, or rather, is it likely that any of these magazines have facts or data which they would withhold just for the sake of being sensational?"

• "Life magazine has a lot of information that we do not have on different sightings. They have some very good sightings too. I mean, they've called in some pretty important people around the United States. They won't, they're very hesitant to tell you who works for them as their consultants. But they have got some pretty good sightings that we have never heard of, and they're going to use those in their article, although they have checked those with us. The two or three old standbys that everybody always plays up, such as this Mantell case down in Kentucky where this guy got killed chasing one of them, supposedly, the one up in Sioux Falls, South Dakota where the F-51 pilot fought with this thing for 15 minutes, and a few of those that are outstanding as far as the science fiction writers are concerned, Life is going to leave out. They're not going to dig those up again and rehash them again."

(Question from audience)

• "Was it ever established what caused Mantell's death and disintegration?"

• "Well, they think, I mean, the official report is, and I tend to believe it, is that he didn't have any oxygen at all, and he just climbed up until he passed out and then the airplane went into a dive and just tore itself to pieces. I think that that probably, what he was chasing is still open to discussion. It was either, probably either Venus or one of these great big Skyhook balloons that General Mills puts up, because there was one lost in the area at the time, although they were never able to say where it was, except that it was

either over Kentucky or Tennessee. That's all they've been able to pin down, and they think that that might have been it. But..."

(Question from audience)

• "Is this still classified top secret, since Life is coming out with it?"

• "No, uh, we've, we actually, we carry it as confidential, the overall project. We're trying to get it dropped down to restricted now because Life is going to come out with a lot of material we've given them that is classified, or was classified at one time. The only time this was classified top secret was right after it came out. We've been carrying this confidential. There are some aspects of it we'll have to keep classified as secret or maybe higher when we start listing Air Defense radar stations, possible tie-in with some of our latest developments and things like that. We'll have to keep that classified. But just, or just the details of a sighting, we're going to try to declassify to restricted because we've had trouble in the past on that. Some newspaper will call up and say, 'Big sighting up somewhere,' and we'll say, 'Yes, we've heard about it.' And they'll say, 'What's the results?' We'll say, 'We can't tell you about that, it's classified.' So immediately they come out with a big story about, 'The Air Force just picked up a spaceship somewhere and they won't tell us about it.' And that's the thing we're trying to get away from. I mean, we don't want to excite anybody on the project."

• "There is one other area that's classified, and that's where we have reports on people. Yes, you know, their background to try to determine whether they're reliable or not. We run into one interesting bit of discussion on this classification because some people who say, 'Well, now, these could be from Russia,' which is true, they could be. 'Therefore, we're doing them a great service reporting them in our papers very carefully where they get plots,' which is true. But we feel that the papers, I mean, when they get one, are going to report it, and then they're going to come to us for what we know on it. And it's inevitable if the papers pick it up. So that's one reason we like this reporting channel that's established, that if anybody sights one of them, it's not too illogical for somebody if he sees something in the air to call the nearest Air Force base. I mean, it's one of the first things he would think of, 'Maybe they've got something in the air.' And we have found, though, just as an example of this T-33 case you mentioned, the reporters are right on hand to discuss this thing with the pilots when they landed, and took pictures of them."

• "We found out that in the New York area, some paper, I couldn't tell you which one it is, monitors VHF, monitors all the air traffic in the area. And I don't know why they do it, but they do. And that's where they picked up that T-33 incident, was monitoring the air traffic. Now, I heard two different stories. One that the newspaper actually has a setup themselves to monitor it. Another one that they have two or three hams in the area alerted to call them if anything happens. But this T-33 pilot did call the tower and told them about it, and the newspapers were right on it. So, we found out one thing, and that is the

newspapers surpass the Air Force in their intelligence channels. They're good. I mean, there's just no getting around it."

(Inaudible talk about Mr. Davis and the President)

• "Well, I actually, it goes a little further than that. I mean, it's a wonderful ally. I think the project has varied in its handling a lot just through a difference of opinion or, you know, changes in opinion. There's been great interest in it and then it would fall away, not too much interest, and then great interest. And that's officially too, as well as the public. We feel that by going right down the line and taking every case we get and trying to get additional facts and encouraging anybody and everybody to give us information, there are a lot of groups that are interested in this. There's a, I don't know whether any of you read the Time article a few weeks ago on the saucers. Well, there's a group out on the West Coast that's in their spare time trying to get all of these cases they can to work on. We feel that that group, if we're quite frank with them, would be very cooperative and help us. I mean, we're not trying to hide anything, we're trying to get help. You do have a problem and how far you go publicly, but I think possibly this Life type article will help if they, if they publish what we expect."

Background:

Two witnesses (father and 6 yr. old daughter) in a rural area first observed and photographed two blue elevated lights in flight approximately a mile away towards town. Witness drove towards objects for better view. Upon arriving at general site, objects converged in flight upon witnesses from left and right to a hovering position viewed from front auto window. Frightened by the event and belief that objects began following them, witness drove rapidly one half mile into town and a mile beyond where objects were no longer observed. Daughter developed a chest rash the nest day.

Narrative:

Thursday 10/15/09 17:50

Drove to Modesto, CA and arrived 19:07 at California Highway Patrol at 4030 Kiernan Ave., only to find the office closed.

Drove the route that reporting witness took on the night of his sighting to familiarize myself with surroundings, abstractions, lighting, traffic, and details included in his report.

Unidentified lights reappear in Erath

By AMANDA KIMBLE
Staff Writer
amanda.kimble@empiretribune.com
Published: Tuesday, October 20, 2009 4:52 PM CDT

Area residents are once again reporting strange lights in the sky above Erath County, and much like the reports that flooded in following a widespread sighting in January 2008, witnesses say the amber glowing orbs are like nothing they've seen before.

In the most recent unexplained sighting, a Hamilton County businessman was greeted by the lights as he left a meeting.

Jerry McAdams, publisher of the Hico News Review and Hico ISD school board member, said he was leaving a board meeting Monday with a fellow board member when they saw two amber lights, which were level with each other and seemed to hover in the sky.

"They (the lights) were low in the sky and disappeared in about five seconds," McAdams said. "Then two more appeared, closer together."

He said the lights disappeared several times and reappeared seconds later. Each time the lights were the same amber color, and appeared at different heights and varying distances apart. McAdams said the lights did not move when they were visible or blink. He also said the lights were not like those typically associated with aircraft.

"They were not red, green or white. They did not flash like on an airplane," he said. "There was no motion. Each time they appeared, they were further to the left. I would say they came and went in three cycles."

McAdams said he could not determine the distance of the lights from his Hamilton County vantage point, but said the lights were to the west, in the direction of Dublin, in the southwest portion of Erath County.

"I have never seen anything like that before," McAdams said. "But I do believe what I saw was like previous (reported) sightings."

Two Dublin area neighbors, who asked to remain anonymous, were in their homes when the men walked out and saw "all kinds of lights, all across the sky" Monday.

The men captured what they saw on a cell phone. The grainy recording offers a glimpse of an amber light that appears in the sky several times, and captures the excitement of the group.

One of the men said they first saw a single ball of light, "not like a flashlight or aircraft," which suddenly spawned several other lights.

"It was like the lights were coming off the first ball (of light) we saw," the man said. "And they kept coming, one after another, and moved in every direction."

The man said the lights were white and amber and the whole spectacle lasted a little more than a minute. He said no sound was associated with the sighting, until jets rushed toward the display.

He also said he is not ready to say he saw an alien aircraft, but does believe the unidentified lights were impressive.

"I don't know what it was, but whatever the lights were, they were truly awesome," he said.

These contacts are at much too a preliminary stage to assess the likelihood of their success or failure.

In spite of the above impediments, significant progress has been made in training and initially deploying BAASS field investigative teams during the fall 2009 months. A large part of the current investigations at BAASS are focused on the Utah ranch and surrounding areas. The BAASS MUFON relationship is being closely monitored especially since the case numbers that MUFON are alerting BAASS with, although improving, are still lower than originally expected. The BAASS database of cases is now larger than any other database owned by UAP organizations in North America. It should be noted that BAASS has initiated a separate Capella database for the events on the Utah ranch and surrounding areas, a report on which will be forthcoming in the coming months.

2. The story by Lionel Shapiro regarding war weapons developed in Spain evidently was printed in a number of leading newspapers throughout the country. The significance of this article will be dependent upon certain essential elements for such alleged important developments, such as funds, materials, experimental testing facilities, and technological "know-how". The latter is supposed to be supplied by German scientists. The German scientists at this Hq indicate that no important scientists from Germany are working in Spain, and those mentioned in this article are not known to them.

3. If possible, therefore, an effort should be made to obtain names, qualifications, or any information that might help to identify the alleged German scientists working in Spain.

4. A brief statement was made in a recent intelligence report from Hq, USAF, AC/AS-2, regarding a flying disc incident in Alaska in September. The close range sighting reported should render a more detailed observation than what was reported, which also suggests a follow-up.

5. It is further requested that this office be advised as to progress being made on the plotting of all flying disc incidents to date, particularly in North America. It was understood that Dr. Carroll was going to plot these incidents, but no further word was received regarding this effort.

SUBJECT: AMC Opinion Concerning "Flying Discs"

TO: Commanding General
Army Air Forces
Washington 25, D. C.
ATTENTION: Brig. General George Schulgen
AC/AS-2

1. As requested by AC/AS-2 there is presented below the considered opinion of this Command concerning the so-called "Flying Discs". This opinion is based on interrogation report data furnished by AC/AS-2 and preliminary studies by personnel of T-2 and Aircraft Laboratory, Engineering Division T-3. This opinion was arrived at in a conference between personnel from the Air Institute of Technology, Intelligence T-2, Office, Chief of Engineering Division, and the Aircraft, Power Plant and Propeller Laboratories of Engineering Division T-3.

2. It is the opinion that:

a. The phenomenon reported is something real and not visionary or fictitious.

b. There are objects probably approximating the shape of a disc, of such appreciable size as to appear to be as large as man-made aircraft.

c. There is a possibility that some of the incidents may be caused by natural phenomena, such as meteors.

d. The reported operating characteristics such as extreme rates of climb, maneuverability (particularly in roll), and action which must be considered evasive when sighted or contacted by friendly aircraft and radar, lend belief to the possibility that some of the objects are controlled either manually, automatically or remotely.

e. The apparent common description of the objects is as follows:-

(1) Metallic or light reflecting surface.

U-39552

SECRET

Basic Ltr fr CG, AMC, WF to CG, AAF, Wash. D. C. subj "AMC Opinion Concerning "Flying Discs".

(2) Absence of trail, except in a few instances when the object apparently was operating under high performance conditions.

(3) Circular or elliptical in shape, flat on bottom and domed on top.

(4) Several reports of well kept formation flights varying from three to nine objects.

(5) Normally no associated sound, except in three instances a substantial rumbling roar was noted.

(6) Level flight speeds normally above 300 knots are estimated.

f. It is possible within the present U. S. knowledge -- provided extensive detailed development is undertaken -- to construct a piloted aircraft which has the general description of the object in subparagraph (e) above which would be capable of an approximate range of 7000 miles at subsonic speeds.

g. Any developments in this country along the lines indicated would be extremely expensive, time consuming and at the considerable expense of current projects and therefore, if directed, should be set up independently of existing projects.

h. Due consideration must be given the following:-

(1) The possibility that these objects are of domestic origin - the product of some high security project not known to AC/AS-2 or this Command.

(2) The lack of physical evidence in the shape of crash recovered exhibits which would undeniably prove the existence of these objects.

(3) The possibility that some foreign nation has a form of propulsion possibly nuclear, which is outside of our domestic knowledge.

3. It is recommended that:-

a. Headquarters, Army Air Forces issue a directive assigning a priority, security classification and Code Name for a detailed study of this matter to include the preparation of complete sets of all available and pertinent data which will then be made available to the Army, Navy, Atomic Energy Commission, JRDB, the Air Force Scientific Advisory Group, NACA, and the RAND and NEPA projects for comments and recommendations, with a preliminary report to be forwarded within 15 days of receipt of the data and a detailed report thereafter every 30 days as the investi-

COMMENT No. 1
Lt Col Garrett/nc/4544
1. From a detailed study of certain reported observations on the flying saucers, selected for their veracity and reliability, it is apparent that several aspects of their appearance have a common pattern.
2. Before pursuing its investigation of these objects any further, this Office requests assurance that no research project of the Army Air Forces, at present being test-flown, has the following characteristics and that it may therefore be assumed the recent flying saucer "mystery" is not of United States origin:
a. Surface is metallic - indicating a metallic skin, at least.
b. When a trail is observed, it is a lightly colored blue-brown haze, similar to a rocket engine's exhaust. Contrary to a rocket of the solid type, one observation indicates that the fuel may be throttled, which would indicate a liquid rocket engine.
c. As to shape, all observations state that the object is circular, or at least elliptical, flat on the bottom and slightly domed on the top.
d. Size estimates place it somewhere near the size of a C-54 or Constellation as they would appear while flying at 10,000'.
e. Some reports describe two tabs located at the rear and symmetrical about the axis of flight motion.
f. Flights have been reported containing from three to nine objects, flying good formation on each other, with speeds always above 300 knots.
g. The discs oscillate laterally while flying along, which could be snaking.

enroute to his office and before entering heard one of the local aircraft in the traffic pattern. Looking up he observed the aircraft and slightly to the left he saw 2 silver objects of either spherical or disc-like shape moving about 300 MPH at approximately 8000 ft heading about 320° due north. He immediately called S/Sgt Gerald E. Bauman, T/Sgt Joseph Ruvolo and Miss Jannette Marie Scotte. Witnesses all verified the sighting and the direction of the objects - all three stated that the objects were moving toward Mojave, Calif.

Witness was sure it was not an optical illusion or that the objects were not weather balloons since they traveled against prevailing wind and since the speed at which they traveled and the horizontal direction taken indicated that they were not weather balloons. Furthermore they could not remain at the same altitude so consistently if they were weather balloons. Witness then attempted to get personnel (medical officers) to further verify the sighting but by the time the additional personnel had arrived at the same the original objects had disappeared due to the speed at which they were traveling. However, two of them sighted a third object of a silver spherical or disc-like nature at approximately 8000 ft traveling in circles over the north end of the airfield. Five out of the seven personnel saw this object. All looked away from the object several times to make sure there was no eye strain. He stated that this object performed too tight a circle to be any type of known aircraft.

Evaluation: Confirmed by other sources.

Statement given by Major J. C. Wise, Test Pilot, Muroc Army Air Field, Muroc, California.

On 7 July 1947, at approximately 10:10, while running up the XP-81 on the ground I noticed everyone was looking up into the air. 26. Remarks:
(over)

On the 8 July 1947 at 11:50 the undersigned was sitting in an observation truck located in Area #3, Rogers Dry Lake, was gazing upward toward a formation of two (2) P-82's and an A-26 aircraft flying at 20,000 feet, preparing to carry out of a seat ejection experiment, when I observed a rounded object, white aluminum in color, which at first resembled a parachute canopy. The first impression was that a premature ejection of the seat and dummy had occurred. This body was ejected at a determined height lower than 20,000 feet, and was falling at three (3) times the rate observed for the parachute which ejected thirty minutes later. As it fell it drifted slightly north of due west against the prevailing wind, toward Mount Wilson. The speed, horizontal motion could not be determined, but appeared slower than the maximum velocity of P-80 aircraft.

As this object descended through a low enough level to permit observation of its lateral silhouette, it presented a distinct ovular outline, with two (2) projections on the upper surface which might have been thick fins or nobs. These crossed each other at intervals, suggesting either rotation or oscillation of slow type.

No smoke flames, propellar arks, engine noise, or other clasuable or visible ears of propulsion were noted. The color was silvery, resembling aluminum painted fabric, and did not appear as dense as a parachute canopy.

When the object dropped to a level such that came into line of vision of the mountain tops, it was lost to the vision of the observer.

It is estimated that the object was in line of vision about 90 seconds. Of the five (5) people sitting in the observation truck, four (4) observed this object and made remarks about it. These people include:

Mr. Lenz - Civilian, Wright Field, Dayton, Ohio.
(Other names not given)

The following is my own personal opinions about this object:

1. I think it was a manmade object, as evidenced distantly by the outline and functional appearance.

2. It's size was not far from 25 feet with a parachute canopy.

3. The path followed by this object appeared as though it might have been dropped from a great height.

Seeing this was not a hallucination or other fancies of a sense.

Whatever they are, there are some disc-like objects flying around in the sky.

Or else eight (8) Portland area policemen and deputy sheriffs who sighted the objects Friday, numerous private citizens, the crew of a United Air Lines plane over Boise, Idaho, and a cosmetic worker who claims to have photographed one near Seattle, are all wrong.

In Portland, the alert was sound over police radio at 1:16 P. M. Friday, after the East Side Station received a score of calls and the discs were overhead. Within seconds, two prowl cars reported chasing the mystery craft.

FLASHES SEEN, NOISE LACKING.

First to report in were Patrolmen Walter Lipsy and Robert Ellis in Car No. 52, who stopped near Ortke Park. Both World War II veteran as and civilian alike, they sighted three of the objects within 30 seconds traveling at great height and speed over the park. They reported they saw no engine noises but saw flashes. The objects seemed erratic and changed direction at flight. The patrolmen agreed but without knowledge of the size of the objects it would be impossible to judge their speed or altitude.

Patrolman Earl Patterson in car No. 41 stopped at nd 33rd Avenue and Foster road to look eastward from where the discs were reported. The craft came in and then coming out of the sun. He saw what appeared to be [illegible] later circumscribed the sky and the rest of the sky and leading westward. The craft seemed to be climbing or gradually when it didn't flash as it did [illegible].

SURVEYING ... INTEREST

A former ground veteran, he said the object was unlike any plane he had ever seen. He thought it was a radio-controlled because it could change direction at a sharp angle without difficulty.

Members of the Bunker Hill at the corner of 14 Irving Street streetcar stop when they heard the all-out alert. Capt. E. A. Dunn, Lieut. Frank H. T. Anstel and Patrolman K. G. Ellis all said the objects could be seen to be going south high over the Glide hills at terrific speed. Capt. Price said the glimpses kept them from a certainty whether there were discs or ships.

"The discs would oscillate and sometimes we would see a full disc, then a half-moon shape, then nothing at all," he reported. The objects looked like a shiny chromium ball on top of a stick which wobbled, dipped red and reappeared.

There was a plane in the sky at the time, but all were emphatic that the discs were not planes.

AIRLINES CREW GIVES CONTRADICTORY ACCOUNTS OF FLYING DISCS. FIVE SEIGHTS.

Circumstantial reports of flying discs in the sky Friday came from the crew of a United Airlines plane over Boise, Idaho, and a second group here at Seattle, as well as from Portland area police and citizens.

E. J. Smith, Chief Pilot of the airliner, who served from the sighted there were approximately a low aircraft which flew about on the bottom and eventually at 10,000 feet. The objects appeared against the sunset. Shortly after the plane took off at 6:50 p. m., he said.

"They then cleared," he reported. "We followed them for about 50 miles, but could not keep up. Finally the objects disappeared. We were unable to tell whether they outdistanced us or disintegrated."

NOT AIRCRAFT.

"We can't say whether they were discs, or what they were. But whatever they were, they were not aircraft, but were at least 10 miles or so distant."

In Seattle, Capt. Ed Hanson of Boeing Field told the United Press that he had seen what appeared to be a "white object" flying high and at a fast speed.

At Mt. Olympic Pictures, New York City, a photographer said he had shown two tiny dots, one of which was clearly visible.

In Oakland, Ill. Chief amusement park official, reported several objects "like shining discs" in the sky Friday. He saw several lights, including one that appeared to be red.

In Vancouver, Wash., Sgt. Walter Sullivan, Chief Mckay and Pvt. Kniess reported the Portland police were out in full force at the Vancouver airport to look at the sky. Over Portland, they said, Sullivan said, they saw several objects "like a flying saucer" and they left a low humming noise.

OTHER VIEWS.

Col. O. R. Dodson, Commander of the Oregon National Guard, made an inspection of the area from the air after the discs were reported. He said he saw nothing "suspicious".

Only three military airplanes in the air at the time were B-17 bombers near Astoria.

Despite all the reports, at least two persons remained unconvinced of the existence of the discs. Al F. Sanford, Hillside Avenue, said it was all the work of some kind of optical illusion.

Dr. Walter Kelley, Jr., of 6600 N. Burrage Avenue, telephoned the Journal to talk to the newspapers for "promoting a hoax". He said he saw objects in the air about 5 minutes after an airplane passed over the house. To him the objects looked like bits of crumpled foil, perhaps cigarette wrappers.

MORE SEEN LATER.

Byers, 1205 Willamette Avenue, said he saw three flying saucers cross the Willamette River near the Rose Island bridge at about 4 p.m., moving in the west, then returned. Ten minutes later they were back in the east for two or three minutes. He said they resembled metallic discs glinting in the sun.

In Hillsboro, Oregon, a group of citizens saw 15 flying saucers hovering over the Hillsboro county airport.

At Vancouver, Wash., Mrs. Lawrence J. Sims, 1204 NE 21st Ave., reported sighting a disc-like object as it was moving in a regular pattern over the Gresham district. She said it seemed to be moving slowly.

DAVID MOUNTAIN.

Thomas W. Dwyer, 1232 NE 55th Avenue, said he sighted two metallic silver objects. They were at least 6 feet in diameter and hovered for about 5 minutes before moving on. He said the objects looked like pie pans and were glistening in the sun.

C. J. Boone, of Vale, Oregon, said he sighted a group of objects at about 7 p.m., with a red glow near the bottom.

S. M. Cox, 2506 NE 65th Avenue, recovered from Rose City golf course a piece of metal about 12 inches long, which he said might be part of one of the discs seen Friday. He said it was of low quality, measured 23-1/2 by 36 inches.

Flight leader called to observe that "object was twelve o'clock high." Asked to describe it, he stated "it is bright and climbing away from me." He stated at first that it was going about 150 MPH. Then Control Tower lost sight of the flight but could still see the object. (In connection with this, Lt Col E. Garrison Wood who witnessed the sighting stated that while it appeared about 1/10 the size of a full moon, if the thing were a great distance away, as compared to the diminishing size of the P-51's flying toward it, it would seem that it was at least several hundred feet in diameter.) Shortly after NS 861, the flight leader, stated that he was "at 15,000 ft and still climbing" He stated that he judged the speed to be the same as his or approx 360 MPH. One of his planes then asked him to level off but no reply was heard from the flight leader. That was the last message received from any member of the flight.

After dark, another or the same object appeared in approx 234° from Godman at 6° elevation. This body moved to the west (259°) and then down. The shape was fluid but generally round with no tail, the color changing from white, to blue, to red to yellow and had a black spot in the center at all times.

At 1600 CST it was obscured by clouds.

NOTE: Later, an astronomer was contacted who attempted to account for this phenomena as either Venus or a comet. (1)

SEE ALSO: Report of civilians and state police and corroborated version on this incident.

We assume the object to be a meteor.

It appeared on a course about 350° true some 5 miles away. The light grew in intensity (but without any change in color) to a point estimated to be one mile off starboard bow of the plane. When the PA plane switched over to manual control the object suddenly veered to an approximate course of 105° and then the bright light appeared to split into two parts and assumed a reddish hue. These two reddish lights did not have the intensity of the white light and appeared about a wing-length apart. As it changed its course the white light and the twin lights appeared to burn out 30 miles ahead. The entire phenomenon was observed for some six seconds. Both observers were questioned as to possibility of optical illusion and the probability that the object dropped at an oblique angle but both firmly declared the object apparently changed course and that it appeared to hold altitude throughout the entire time observed.

PAA plane was eastbound from Midway on magnetic course 96, which is approximately 110° true, and flying at 9,000 feet at about 205 knots. SUBJECT: SUMMARY OF AERIAL PHENOMENA IN NEW MEXICO
MISCELLANEOUS - INFORMATION CONCERNING
PURPOSE
To advise that: (1) OSI has expressed concern in connection with the continued appearance of unexplained phenomena described as green fireballs, discs and meteors in the vicinity of sensitive installations in New Mexico. (2) Dr. LaPaz, Meteor Expert of the University of New Mexico, reported that the phenomena does not appear to be of meteoric origin. (3) OSI has contracted with Land-Air Inc., Alamogordo, New Mexico, to make scientific study of the unexplained phenomena.
NATURE OF PHENOMENA
Observations of aerial phenomena occurring within the vicinity of sensitive installations have been recorded by the Air Force since December, 1948. The phenomena have been classified into 3 general types which are identified as follows:
1. Green fireballs, objects moving at high speed in shapes resembling half moons, circles and discs emitting green light.
2. Discs, round flat shaped objects or phenomena moving at fast velocity and emitting a brilliant white light or reflected light.
3. Meteors, aerial phenomena resembling meteoric material moving at high velocity and varying in color.
The above phenomena have been reported to vary in color from brilliant white to amber, red and green.
Since 1948, approximately 150 observations of aerial phenomena referred to above have been recorded in the vicinity of installations in New Mexico. A number of observations have been reported by different reliable individuals at approximately the same time.

RESULTS OF AN INQUIRY BY PROFESSOR LINCOLN LA PAZ
Dr. LaPaz, Director, Institute of Meteoritics, University of New Mexico, submitted an analysis of the various observations on May 23, 1950. He concluded, as a result of his investigation, that approximately half of the phenomena recorded were of meteoric origin. The other phenomena commonly referred to as green fireballs or discs he believed to be U.S. guided missiles being tested in the neighborhood of the installations. Dr. LaPaz pointed out that if he were wrong in interpreting the phenomena as originating with U.S. guided missiles that a systematic investigation of the observations should be made immediately. Dr. LaPaz pointed out that missiles moving with the velocities of the order of those found for the green fireballs and discs could travel from the Ural region of the USSR to New Mexico in less than 15 minutes. He suggested that the observations might be of guided missiles launched from bases in the Urals.
On the basis of the investigations made by Dr. LaPaz and the Air Force, it was concluded that the occurrence of the unexplained phenomena in the vicinity of sensitive installations was a cause for concern. The Air Force entered into a contract with Land-Air, Incorporated, Alamogordo, New Mexico, for the purpose of making scientific studies of the green fireballs and discs. It was pointed out in the summary furnished by OSI on July 19, 1950, that the unexplained green fireballs and discs are still observed in the vicinity of sensitive military and Government installations.
RESULTS OF AIR FORCE INVESTIGATION
The Air Force together with Land-Air, Incorporated, have established a number of observation posts in the vicinity of Vaughn, New Mexico, for the purpose of photographing and determining the speed, height and nature of the unusual phenomena referred to as green fireballs and discs. On May 24, 1950, personnel of Land-Air, Incorporated, sighted 8 to 10 objects of aerial phenomena. A 24-hour day watch is being maintained and has been designated "Project Twinkle."
- 2 -

CONCLUSIONS
The Albuquerque Office, in a letter dated August 10, 1950, advised that there have been no new developments in connection with the efforts to ascertain the identity of the strange aerial phenomena referred to as green fireballs and discs. The Albuquerque Office advised that Dr. Anthony O. Mirarchi, Project Engineer, had been informed of the Bureau's jurisdiction relative to espionage and sabotage and arrangements have been made so that the Bureau will be promptly advised in the event additional information relative to this project indicates any jurisdiction on the part of the Bureau.
ACTION
None. The above is for your information.

SUBJECT: FLYING SAUCERS

DATE: September 27, 1950

SAC Cornelius of Philadelphia called at 10:45 A.M. today and stated that yesterday evening while two officers of the Philadelphia Police Department were cruising in their scout car they saw through the windshield an object descending slowly to the earth which appeared at first glance to be a parachute.

When the officers first noticed the object, it was at tree-top level and was described as being six feet in diameter. It landed in a field near-by and the officers, upon examining it, noted that it gave out a purplish glow which was almost a mist. The officers summoned two other police officers. After looking at the object for some time they attempted to pick it up. The object broke, leaving a slight odorless residue. Over a period of about 25 minutes which the officers spent watching the object it completely disintegrated. The officers further commented that the object was so light that when it hit the field, it did not even bend the weeds or the grass it fell on.

Mr. Cornelius said that he has called the local office of the Air Force but the individual with whom he spoke there said he knew nothing about them and was not aware that his office was looking into reports of this type.

Mr. Cornelius desired to know what further action should be taken by him.

I told Mr. Cornelius that he was correct in referring this matter to the local office of OSI and that he should direct a letter to the Bureau incorporating all available information concerning the matter and that we here, upon its receipt, in turn would bring it to the attention of OSI Headquarters.

1. The United States Air Force has a continuing requirement for the reporting and technical analysis of observations of unconventional aircraft which might indicate an advance in technological progress of a foreign power. An unconventional aircraft, within the meaning of this directive, is defined as any aircraft or airborne object which by performance, aerodynamic characteristics, or unusual features, does not conform to any presently known aircraft type.

2. It is desired that information on unconventional aircraft be reported in the following manner:

a. A separate report of each incident will be forwarded. No information other than that bearing on the unconventional aircraft will be included in this report.

b. Priority of transmission accorded the report will be that appropriate in the judgment of the forwarding agency, according to its apparent authenticity and importance as intelligence.

c. Reports will be forwarded to Commanding General, Air Materiel Command, Attention: MCIS.

d. Reports forwarded by electrical transmission will include, as far as possible:

(1) A brief description of the object(s); its shape, size, color, number, formation if more than one, aerodynamic features, trail or exhaust, propulsion system, speed, sound, maneuvers, manner of disappearance, and other pertinent or unusual features.

(2) Time sighted in 24-hour clock zonal time, and length of time observed.

(5) Identifying information on observer(s) and witnesses, estimate of reliability and experience, and any factors bearing on estimated reliability of the sighting.

(6) Weather and wind conditions (teletype sequences) at time and place of sightings.

e. Reports forwarded by electrical transmission will be followed up within ten (10) days by a written report on AF Form 112. FLYING SAUCERS

During the late evening hours of September 26, 1950, two Philadelphia police officers observed a peculiar phenomenon on Vare Boulevard near 26th Street when they saw a round object about six feet in circumference slowly float down to the ground.

The object had the appearance of a parachute and landed in a field, it being so light it did not even depress the weeds in the field. The object was lavender in color, described by the officers as dewy, sort of like soap suds, and evaporating within fifteen or twenty minutes after it landed. When touched by the officers, the substance composing the object disappeared, leaving nothing but a slight sticky substance.

This matter was reported to this office by the Philadelphia Police and for that matter, was subsequently carried in the Philadelphia press as "Flying Saucer Just Dissolves".

Mr. LAUGHLIN of the Bureau was telephonically advised of the above by this office and issued instructions that the matter should be referred to Air Force Intelligence for handling and any investigation. Accordingly, Major WATTS of the Philadelphia Office of OSI was telephonically advised of the above and no further action was taken by this office.

There is attached, as a part of this summary, a compilation of aerial phenomena sightings that have occurred mostly in the New Mexico area and have been reported by this District Office subsequent to December 1948. This compilation of sightings is not a complete record of all reported observations, but includes only those in which sufficient information was available to justify their inclusion. The observers of these phenomena include scientists, Special Agents of the Office of Special Investigations (IG) USAF, airline pilots, military pilots, Los Alamos Security Inspectors, military personnel, and many other persons of various occupations whose reliability is not questioned. This compilation sets forth the most important characteristics with respect to each observation and evaluates each sighting into one of three classifications, (1) green fireball phenomenon, (2) disc or variation, and (3) probably meteoric.

Subject: Anomalous Luminous Phenomena (Seventh Report)

     1.  In the second report of this series, dated 1948, December 20, the
writer listed ten significant differences between the bright green horizon-
tally-moving fireballs observed in the interval 1948, December 5-20, and
typical meteors. These differences were the following:

     (1) The horizontal nature of the paths of most of the December
fireballs is most unusual. Genuine meteors are rarely observed to move
in horizontal paths.

     (2) Again the very low height of the December fireball discussed
in section 2 above sets it off in sharp contrast from the genuine
meteors for which heights of the order of 40 or more miles are nor-
mally observed.

     (3) The velocity determined for the fireball of December 12 is
much less than the velocities determined from typical meteors (and
yet is considerably greater than the speeds of the V-2 Rockets or
jet planes or of conventional flares).

     (4) In the case of meteorites that penetrate to as low levels
as that determined for the fireball of December 12, the observed lu-
minous phenomena are always accompanied by very violent noises. No
noises whatever have been observed in connection with the various
December fireballs so far investigated. (Note added on 1950, May 23:
Possible exceptions to the noiselessness of green fireballs are the
incidents of 1949, January 30, and 1949, December 4.)

     (5) Genuine meteors normally show remarkable variations in
brightness, beginning as fine thin hair lines, which are scarcely
visible to the observer, and then brightening up to flash out near
the end of their paths. In the case of the December fireballs most
of the observers have reported that the green balls appeared almost
instantly at their full brightness.

CONFIDENTIAL

Subj: Anomalous Luminous Phenomena (Seventh Report)        May 23, 1950

     (6) In the case of genuine meteors the paths are directed to-
ward all points of the compass with equal frequency. On the contrary
in the case of the green fireballs, plots of admissible approach sec-
tors show that there is a very pronounced tendency for the paths to
come in from the north half of the sky.

     (7) The three groups of anomalous greenish luminous phenomena
show a curious association with well known meteor showers, although
none of these meteor showers normally produce extremely bright green
fireballs, such as those recently observed. For example, the obser-
vation mentioned by Mr. Konnig appeared near the maximum of the
Quadrantid shower of early January, Mr. McCullough's observation of
August was near the time of the Persid shower and the December
observations all fell in the interval covered by the Geminid shower.
This relationship might indicate an attempt to render the green fire-
balls less conspicuous by causing them to appear only when there is
considerable meteoric activity.

     (8) As noted in an earlier communication, the remarkably vivid
green color reported for most of the December fireballs is rarely
observed in the case of genuine meteors. By laboratory test this
peculiar color seems to be identical with that given off by copper
salts in the blowpipe flame. If this identification is correct,
the wave length of the radiation from the green fireballs is near
λ =5218Å.

     (9) The duration estimates of between 2 and 3 seconds reported
for the green fireballs are considerably longer than those (0.4 -
0.5 seconds) for the ordinary visual meteors, but shorter than the
duration estimates invariably reported in the case of a genuine
meteorite fall (5 to 30 seconds or even longer).

     (10) For none of the green fireballs has a train of sparks or
a dust cloud been reported. This contrasts sharply with the be-
havior noted in case of meteoric fireballs--particularly those
that penetrate to the very low levels where the green fireball of
December 12 was observed.

     2.  In the year and a half since this list was prepared, many ad-
ditional observations have been made, the total number of objects now
accepted as belonging in the green fireball category being 72. (Al-
though this number constitutes nearly 50% of the incidents listed in the
accompanying Summary, it constitutes less than 5% of the total number of
unscreened observations reported to the writer.) Critical analysis of
all green fireball reports now available shows that only one of the
statements in the list given in paragraph 1 needs to be modified,
namely, item (1). Within the last year, a considerable number of the
green fireballs have appeared to fall vertically downward rather than

to move horizontally. However, a strictly vertical infall is also very
rarely observed in the case of genuine meteor falls.

     3.  An analysis just completed of the time distribution of the green
fireballs so far observed permits us to add an 11th item to the list of
differences given in paragraph 1 above. The graph of frequency versus
local time which accompanies the present report shows that the maximum
frequency of sighting of green fireballs (occurring at approximately
2030) coincides in time with neither the frequency maximum for ordinary
meteors (occurring at approximately 0300) nor the frequency maximum for
meteorite falls (occurring at approximately 1600).

     4.  Inspection of the graph referred to in paragraph 3 also will
show that most of the green fireballs have been sighted in a time inter-
val extending from about 5 p.m. to 11 p.m. (MST). This concentration
might be even more pronounced if it were possible to screen out of the
secondary maximum, around 2 a.m. (MST), all ordinary meteors which have
been mistakenly identified as green fireballs. That such misidentifica-
tion has occurred is strongly suggested by the near coincidence in time
of the secondary maximum of the green fireballs and the well established
early morning maximum of the ordinary meteors.

     5.  Some significance may attach to the fact that the time interval
alluded to in paragraph 4 extends from about 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. in the Ural
region of the USSR. Since missiles moving with velocities of the order
of those found for the green fireballs for which real path determinations
have been possible would travel from the southern Urals to New Mexico in
less than 15 minutes, a possible interpretation of the concentration of
sightings referred to in paragraph 4 is that the green fireballs result
from guided missiles launched from bases in the Urals in the morning
hours before cloudiness due to convection or blinding afternoon dust
storms can interfere with non-radar tracking, such as has been used by
the Optical Trajectory Section at White Sands Proving Ground.

     6.  There is also a pronounced concentration of green fireball
incidents on the four days, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday, almost
all of the most widely observed incidents having occurred on Saturday
or Sunday.

     7.  It is a curious and fairly well-established fact that there
has been a distinct decline in the number of green fireball sightings
during the last two months, within which the number of so-called "fly-
ing saucer" incidents in this region has attained an all-time high.

     8.  Although I have recently received from Dr. Joseph Kaplan of the
Scientific Advisory Board a letter containing the statement "Frankly, I
don't know of any U. S. experiments that would result in the appearance
of these unconventional objects, and neither does Von Karman". I still

consider the most probable explanation of the green fireballs to be the
one given in the first of the three paragraphs below which are quoted
from my letter of 1950, February 20, to Dr. P. H. Wyckoff, Chief Atmos-
pheric Physics Laboratory, Base Directorate for Geophysical Research.
The last two paragraphs quoted below well summarize my recommendations
concerning the green fireball problem:

     "As a preliminary to setting down the project recommendations
which you requested, I have very carefully reviewed all available
fireball data (observers' reports, transit measurements, calculated
real paths, etc.) covering incidents from those of December 5, 1948
to the extraordinary incident of February 7, 1950, which has been
under intensive investigation for the last two weeks. As a result
of this comprehensive review, particularly as it relates to the in-
cident of February 7, 1950, I feel compelled to write you in some-
what different terms concerning my own part in the proposed fireball
project than I had in mind when we last discussed this matter. In
brief, I have come to the conclusion that, on the basis of the
evidence now available to me, I would not be justified in recommend-
ing a fireball project. In my opinion, this evidence proves conclu-
sively that the fireballs reported on fall into one of two categories:
Those of the first category (the majority) are meteorite falls of
unusual, but certainly not of impossible, magnitude, frequency and
other characteristics; those of the second category (the minority)
are U. S. guided missiles undergoing tests in the neighborhoods of
the sensitive installations they are designed to defend. This
interpretation of the latter category is the one that I proposed in
answer to a question raised by Dr. Teller at the first Los Alamos
conference on February 17, 1949. It was not taken seriously then
and I doubt that it will be taken seriously at the present time.
However, even if my interpretation of the unconventional fireballs
is the correct one, it is obvious that those in position to confirm
it should refuse to do so."

     "Only one other point need be stressed, namely, that if I am
wrong in interpreting the guided missiles as of U. S. origin, then
certainly intensive, systematic investigation of these objects
should not be delayed until the termination of the present academic
year. Recent international developments compel one to sense the
imperative necessity of immediate investigation of the unconvention-
al green fireballs, in case you are in possession of information
proving that they are not U. S. missiles."

     "If such an immediate investigation were to be undertaken, I
would recommend that Dr. Fred L. Whipple, of Harvard College Obser-
vatory, be placed in charge of the photographic phase of the inves-
tigation; that Dr. Peter M. Millman, of the Dominion Observatory,
be placed in charge of the spectrographic phase of the investigation;

Photograph of Unknown Aerial Phenomena taken at Datil, New Mexico by Cpl Lertis E. Stanfield, Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico on 24 and 25 Feb 1950. An analysis of the above photograph was made by Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, Head of the Institute of Meteoritics, University of New Mexico, Albuquerque, New Mexico, who reached the following conclusions:

a. The angular diameter of the perfectly round luminous object Stanfield observed was approximately 1/4 of a degree.

b. The angular velocity of the object in the sky was greater than half a degree per minute.

Dr. LaPaz stated that on the basis of the results (a) and (b) above, the object seen by Stanfield was not the moon (for the angular diameter is too small), it was not Venus or any other planet (for the angular diameter was too large), and it was not a bright fixed star slightly out of focus (for the observed rate of motion is double that due to the diurnal rotation of the earth).

DENVER--A CONSTRUCTION WORKER AT LOS ALAMOS, N.M., HAS REPORTED THAT A STRANGE "BLINKING OBJECT" SOARED OVER A HIGHLY RESTRICTED AREA OF THE BIG ATOMIC ENERGY CENTER.

LEE ROBINSON OF THE ARMEX CONSTRUCTION COMPANY SENT THE DENVER POST A COPY OF A MIMEOGRAPHED FORM WHICH HE USED TO REPORT THE OBJECT TO THE AEC.

THE FORMS ARE PREPARED BY THE AEC FOR "REPORTS OF UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL OBJECTS AT LOS ALAMOS."

THE ORIGINAL THREE-PAGE REPORT, ROBINSON SAID, WAS SUBMITTED TO THE ATOMIC ENERGY SECURITY SERVICE SEPT. 12., THE DAY ROBINSON AND EIGHT OTHER EMPLOYEES OF THE ARMEX COMPANY SAY THEY SAW THE OBJECT.

ROBINSON SAID HE AND THE OTHERS WERE EATING LUNCH WHEN THE UNIDENTIFIED OBJECT PASSED OVER. HE SAID IT "WAS NOT A BALLOON OR A CONVENTIONAL TYPE OF AIRCRAFT."

ROBINSON SAID THE OBJECT APPEARED TO BE AT AN ALTITUDE OF ABOUT 20,00 FEET. IT ALTERNATELY FLASHED BRIGHT AND BLACK AT INTERVALS OF TWO SECONDS, HE SAID, AND WAS VISIBLE FOR THREE MINUTES AND 40 SECONDS.

THE SPECIALLY MIMEOGRAPHED FORMS INDICATED THE AEC IS HIGHLY CONCERNED WITH UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL OBJECTS OVER THE PROJECT. THE FORMS CONTAIN SPACES FOR INFORMANTS TO REPORT ON LUMINOSITY OF OBJECT, APPARENT MEANS OF SUPPORT AND PROPULSION AND "ODOR" OF THE OBJECT.

SUBJECT: FLYING SAUCERS

DATE: October 19, 1950

The matter of flying saucers was discussed by Special Agent Edward S. Sanders with Major General Joseph F. Carroll of OSI on October 16, 1950, at which time General Carroll advised that insofar as he has been able to determine the Air Force is not working on any type of "flying saucer" or "flying disk". General Carroll stated that the Air Force is working on high altitude rockets and jet aircraft. He stated these experiments may account for some of the reports concerning flying saucers but that the Air Force is not apparently working on anything which is the cause of the many flying saucers reports. He stated that the Air Force program for investigating reports concerning flying saucers, etc., has been reinstituted at Wright Field and that any pertinent information of interest coming to his attention will be furnished to the Bureau.
